meta.title: FAQ: hiring hypjam and joining the roster | hypjam
meta.description: Answers for brands hiring a UGC agency — pricing, usage rights, turnaround, casting — and for creators joining the roster: equipment, pay, ownership.

hero.p: Everything brands ask before a first brief and everything creators ask before a first shoot. If yours is not here, book a call or email us and a person replies.

items.q: What does it cost?
items.a: Packages start at £1,800 a month for six videos (Starter). Growth is from £3,600 for twelve, and Scale from £6,500 for twenty-four or more. Ad spend, product units and postage are separate, and we scope the final number on the call.

items.q: What is UGC, and how is it different from influencer marketing?
items.a: UGC is content made to a brief, for a flat fee, that you license to run as an ad from your own account or the creator's. Influencer marketing rents someone's audience. We make the former: the creator's following does not matter, the take does.

items.q: How fast do videos turn around?
items.a: Your first cuts arrive within 14 days of a signed brief, with casting, shooting and editing inside that, and your revision round follows. Rush timelines are possible; we will tell you honestly if the brief needs longer.

link.label: See the process week by week

items.q: What do we have to do?
items.a: Sign off the brief and script, pick the hooks with us, approve the creator shortlist, send product (or a login, for an app) and give one round of notes on the cuts. We do the rest.

items.q: What usage rights do we get?
items.a: Organic and paid usage is included as standard for the term of your package. If you need whitelisting or a longer usage window, we build it into the brief upfront so there is no scramble later.

items.q: Which platforms do you shoot for?
items.a: TikTok, Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts, Snapchat and Pinterest, plus Meta ads. We brief and edit natively for wherever the video is actually going to run, not one size fits all.

items.q: How many revisions are included?
items.a: One full revision round per video, in every package. Most rounds get spent on pacing or captions rather than reshoots, because the script is locked before anyone films.

items.q: How does casting work?
items.a: We cast from our own roster against your brief: tone, look, niche, whatever matters for the product. You approve the shortlist before anyone shoots.

items.q: Do we need to send product to creators?
items.a: Usually, yes: one unit per creator cast, posted to the addresses we give you once the shortlist is approved. Apps and software need a working login instead. The brief says exactly what is needed and when.

items.q: Can we use our own founder, or a creator we already work with?
items.a: Yes. Founder-led video is one of our formats: we direct you through the same hooks, retakes and notes as the roster. If you already have a creator you like, we can brief and direct them too.

items.q: How do you handle claims and brand safety?
items.a: Creators only say what the brief has cleared. You approve every script before filming, and if a claim needs evidence we ask for it before the script is locked. Paid content is labelled as paid, following the ASA's CAP Code.

items.q: Do you run the ads as well?
items.a: No. On Growth and Scale we set up whitelisting and Spark Ads, and we tell you which cuts to run where. Your ad spend and your ad account stay with you.

items.q: Is there a minimum term?
items.a: Packages run month to month with a one-month minimum, so you are not locked into a long contract just to find out whether it works.

items.q: Who owns the final videos?
items.a: You license them for the usage window in your package, for organic and paid use. We handle the paperwork with creators so the rights are clean, not implied.

items.q: How do creators get paid?
items.a: We pay creators directly out of your package fee. One contract, one invoice, and no separate negotiations with each creator on your end.

items.q: You're new. Why should we trust you?
items.a: We are new, and we'd rather say so than invent a client list. What you can check instead: the example ads and the 14-day sprint on our home page, and three terms written into every contract: first cuts 14 days after a signed brief; eight hooks written for every script, ready to test; and one contract and one invoice. Nothing is filmed until you've approved the script and the creators, and packages run month to month with a one-month minimum.

items.q: What happens on the call?
items.a: Thirty minutes on Google Meet with Avi. Bring your product and two or three ads you like, yours or anyone's. You'll leave knowing whether UGC suits your launch, which formats we'd test first and why, and what your first month would cost. If another route suits you better, we'll say so.

items.q: Do I need professional equipment?
items.a: No. Your phone is genuinely enough. What matters is that you can act naturally on camera and follow a script without sounding like you are reading one.

items.q: Do I need a big following?
items.a: No. This is not influencer marketing: brands are paying for the content itself, not your audience, so your follower count does not decide whether you are cast.

items.q: How much creative freedom do I get?
items.a: You get a script and direction, but we want your delivery, timing and personality in there too. Directed, not read word for word.

items.q: Who owns the content I shoot?
items.a: The brand licenses it for the usage window agreed before you film, and we spell that out upfront. Organic-only jobs and whitelisted Spark Ads pay and license differently.

items.q: How often will I get briefed?
items.a: It depends on how many brand briefs match your niche, look and availability, so we cannot promise a set number. When a brief fits you, we ask; you can always say no.

items.q: Do I need to be in the UK?
items.a: hypjam is in London, but the roster is mostly remote. Most briefs need a phone, decent light and a bit of space to film.

band.h2: Anything else, ask on the call.
band.p: 30 minutes with Avi, free, on Google Meet. No deck.
